ev.q: This analysis measured progress toward the WHO 2030 vaccination coverage goal of ≥90% completion of the HPV vaccination series among girls by age 15 years.
Human Papillomavirus Vaccination Coverage Among Adolescent Girls Aged 13–17 Years
Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines prevent most cervical cancers and are recommended for girls at age 11–12 years.
This analysis measured progress toward the WHO 2030 vaccination coverage goal of ≥90% completion of the HPV vaccination series
This is the first comprehensive report of trends in HPV vaccination coverage among adolescent girls
Patient-level data from jurisdictional immunization information systems (IISs) were aggregated at the jurisdiction level for this retrospective analysis.

equity.level_reason: Results are by jurisdiction (geography, not an SPD); age and sex only define the population. Out-of-school girls are raised only as a health equity consideration and recommendation, not analyzed.

level_alternative.reason: School enrollment is cited from external sources and may not count as an SES dimension; the 'disparities' are between jurisdictions, which is geography.

equity.equity_measurement: Disparities are between jurisdictions (U.S. territories vs freely associated nations), explained by VFC eligibility, vaccine supply and school-only access; geography and policy status are not SPDs. Guam excluded.

notes: No tests or CIs; the projection that American Samoa will reach 90% by 2025 is a simple extrapolation of the latest annual increase. Active-patient exclusion rules are data cleaning, not procedures. Design inferred as monitoring against the WHO target, plus trend.
view_issues: The WHO goal is completion by age 15 years, but coverage is measured among girls aged 13–17 years, so comparison with the goal is approximate. Summary 'disparities' refers to jurisdictions, not social groups.
